title: Confirmed Axial Orientation but Unresolved Cause: A Response to Landler et al. (2026)
content:
ABSTRACT

Yosef et al. (2022) reported north–south orientation in free-ranging Indian leopards Panthera pardus fusca, particularly during defecation, and interpreted it as evidence of magnetic alignment. Landler et al. (2026) reanalysed these observations to illustrate methodological challenges in studies of animal alignment. Their results supported an axial orientation pattern but also suggested possible influences of roads and spatial factors. In this response, we acknowledge shortcomings in our original analysis and interpretation and examine limitations of Landler et al.'s approach. We focus on model selection, angular reference systems and spatial autocorrelation. We argue that neither magnetic sensitivity nor environmental influences have been established as the cause of the observed pattern. The axial orientation is supported, but its underlying mechanism remains unresolved.
author:
Jakub Z. Kosicki, 
Reuven Yosef
